content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?Apollo Saturn-203 mission launched in 1966Summarized by AI from the post belowNASA MANNED SPACE · JoinMitchell Rothman · Admin · July 5, 2025 · Shared with Public groupManned Space History:59 years ago today in 1966, Apollo Saturn-203 (AS-203) lifted off from Launch Complex 37, Eastern Test Range, at 10:53 a.m. EDT in the second of three Apollo-Saturn missions scheduled before any manned flight in the Apollo program.The first orbital test of the Saturn IB, the primary goals of the AS-203 mission, included observing and testing the behavior of the super cold liquid hydrogen fuel in the rocket’s S-IVB second stage. A slightly modified version served as the third stage in the larger Saturn V Moon rocket and engineers needed to understand the behavior of liquid hydrogen in microgravity to ensure that the stage’s engine would restart once in orbit – a function critical to the success of lunar missions. The flight did not carry an Apollo spacecraft, the rocket was topped off instead by an aerodynamic nose cone. The six-and-a-half-hour AS-203 mission met all of its objectives.In the NASA image below on the left, technicians place the second stage and instrument unit of the AS-203 Saturn IB launch vehicle in place above the first stage at the Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 37 at Cape Kennedy Air Force Station, now Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, in Florida.
